documents.unit: Office of the VP for AI (ai.psu.edu)
documents.title: General Guidelines for AI Use at Penn State
documents.stance_why: The page says only that 'Students should check with instructors' about disclosure or restrictions and that Penn State 'supports the responsible exploration and use of AI'; it neither bans nor requires AI, so stance is delegates.
documents.summary: Short university-wide guidelines from the Office of the VP for AI: obey law, check disclosure rules with instructors, verify output, plus rules on accessibility review, AI-assisted grading approval and copyright. It sets no student-use stance of its own and sends disclosure and use decisions to instructors, supervisors and editors.

units.why: The opening line sets the university's stance as support for 'responsible exploration and use of AI', a purpose statement, so P56 (institution-level framework) fits; it is not a rule on a specific use.
units.anchor: Penn State supports the responsible exploration and use of AI.

units.why: States the scope and purpose of the guidelines ('a shared foundation... informed decisions'), which is a framework preamble (P56); it leaves decisions to individuals.
units.anchor: These general guidelines provide a shared foundation to help the Penn State community make informed

units.why: 'Be sure to follow applicable state and federal laws' (FERPA, HIPAA, GLBA follow in the list) is a duty to comply with existing law when using AI, which is P77 rather than P50, since it does not itself address protecting data in prompts.
units.anchor: Be sure to follow applicable state and federal laws, including, but not limited to:

units.why: Tells users to find out whether AI use must be disclosed; it does not require disclosure itself but points to disclosure rules set elsewhere, so P24 is the nearest type and the check-with-others nature is noted.
units.anchor: Determine if you need to disclose your use of AI or if there are other
units.fit_note: It does not require disclosure; it tells users to determine whether disclosure or other restrictions apply, leaving the answer to instructors, supervisors or editors.

units.why: 'Students should check with instructors' directs students to ask the instructor about disclosure or restrictions before relying on AI, which is P10; the decision is delegated to instructors.
units.anchor: Students should check with instructors

units.why: 'Staff should check with their supervisors' is the staff counterpart of the ask-first rule; P10 is the nearest type though it is about staff and supervisors, not students and instructors.
units.anchor: Staff should check with their supervisors
units.fit_note: Addresses staff and supervisors, not students asking an instructor.

units.why: 'Researchers should check with journal editors' defers to venue rules for AI in scholarship, which is exactly P62's deferral to venue or funder rules.
units.anchor: Researchers should check with journal editors

units.why: 'Be sure to verify the AI output' tells users to check what AI produces, matching P31.
units.anchor: Be sure to verify the AI output

units.why: This sub-item of verifying output asks users to check AI output for 'bias, discrimination, and other ethical issues'; P31 covers biased output that must be critically evaluated; P53 is about naming concerns, not about checking output.
units.anchor: Check for bias, discrimination, and other ethical issues

units.why: Asks users to check accuracy and that citations are to 'real sources', i.e., guarding against hallucinated output, which is P31.
units.anchor: Check that it is accurate, reliable, and contains appropriate citations to real sources

units.why: Points to a separate statement of Penn State's 'AI and ethics values'; the page itself gives no ethical content, so P53 is the nearest type with a note.
units.anchor: For more detailed guidelines and information about ethical use of AI
units.fit_note: A pointer to an ethics values page rather than a statement of specific bias, harm or environmental concerns.

units.why: Refers researchers to separate guidance for AI in research ('best practices and guidance for researchers'), a P62 research-and-scholarship rule pointer.
units.anchor: See Generative AI in Research for best practices and guidance for researchers.
units.fit_note: Pointer only; the research rules are not stated here.

units.why: States that AI tools 'can create barriers for some users', the access concern behind the accessibility rules; P51 covers access and accommodations.
units.anchor: AI tools vary in their level of accessibility, which can create barriers for some users.
units.fit_note: Concerns disability accessibility of tools rather than cost.

units.why: A tool used by several people in a class needs an accessibility review 'required before use', an equity-and-access rule, so P51; it restricts group use until review.
units.anchor: an accessibility review is required before use to comply with Policy AD69
units.fit_note: A required accessibility review for group-used tools, not a cost or optional-use rule.

units.why: If a review finds gaps, an EEAAP 'will be required', which is an alternative-access obligation and fits P51's 'alternatives exist'.
units.anchor: an Enterprise
units.fit_note: Requires an alternative access plan when accessibility gaps are found.

units.why: 'You must still submit an EEAAP... even if the tool is listed' says pre-reviewed status does not remove the obligation; same accessibility-access type as the other EEAAP rules but a distinct rule.
units.anchor: You must still submit an EEAAP for your specific use case, even if the tool
units.fit_note: Pre-reviewed tools still need a use-specific alternative access plan.

units.why: States that accommodation requests 'must be individually evaluated', an accommodation rule matching P51's accommodations clause.
units.anchor: All requests for disability related accommodations must be individually evaluated in accordance with Federal law.
units.fit_note: General disability accommodation rule, not specific to AI.

units.why: 'You must still ensure that the tool is approved for the information' ties tool use to data classification, protecting confidential data and using approved tools, which is P50.
units.anchor: You must still ensure that the tool is approved for the information that you're putting

units.why: Software that assists with grading counts as courseware, and instructors 'need to secure approval' first, so this governs instructor AI use for teaching work (P59); P46 is about who assigns grades, which a later unit covers.
units.anchor: Instructors need to secure approval prior to using courseware
units.fit_note: An approval requirement for AI-assisted grading software.

units.why: Names who must approve AI-assisted grading software ('both the department head and dean'), which is an instructor-AI-use approval chain, so P59 with a note.
units.anchor: approval is needed (email is sufficient) from both the department head and dean
units.fit_note: Specifies the approval chain for AI-assisted grading software.

units.why: Requires AI-assisted grading to follow an existing Senate policy, a comply-with-existing-policy rule (P77).
units.anchor: Any use of software to assist with grading must comply with Senate Policy 47-20 Basis

units.why: 'Instructors must assign grades based on their professional judgment' keeps grading with humans even when tools assist, matching P46.
units.anchor: Instructors must assign grades based on their professional judgment of student achievement.

units.why: Requires human review and verification when tools assist with grading, so humans remain responsible for grades (P46).
units.anchor: instructors must review student work and verify grade accuracy

units.why: Explains the consequence of skipping instructor review ('students could successfully appeal grades'), supporting the human-grading rule (P46), and noting a student appeal route.
units.anchor: Without proper instructor review, students could successfully appeal grades
units.fit_note: States the appeal consequence of unreviewed AI-assisted grading.

units.why: Says AI output 'does not automatically carry unrestricted usage rights', a copyright and ownership fact (P52).
units.anchor: AI-generated content—including text and images—does not automatically carry unrestricted usage rights.

units.why: Warns that training data 'include copyrighted material', which complicates using outputs, a licensing and copyright concern (P52).
units.anchor: Many AI tools are built on datasets that include copyrighted material

units.why: Names Adobe Firefly as 'Penn State's approved image generation tool' for distributed images; this is a sanctioned university tool (P17), chosen over P50 because the stated reason is licensing, not data protection.
units.anchor: use Adobe Firefly, Penn State's approved image generation tool
units.fit_note: Sanctioned tool specified for distributed images for licensing reasons, not for coursework.

units.why: Images from other tools 'should not be used in distributed or published University materials' without consulting staff, a licensing rule (P52).
units.anchor: should not be used in distributed or published University materials without first consulting

units.why: The checklist lists 'including a syllabus statement about AI' as a preparation step, which is P09 (AI statement in the syllabus).

documents.title: Academic Integrity (Engineering faculty/staff)

documents.summary: College of Engineering academic-integrity page that requires every syllabus to state an integrity policy and encourages faculty to list AI details, pointing to university statements and icons. Whether AI is a violation is left to each instructor's course policy.

units.why: 'Faculty are required to state their expectations for academic honesty... in every course' requires a syllabus integrity statement; AI is not named here, so the fit is partial.
